description:
Exclude history files from `jit search` when no file selection is given, using one declaration of the history paths.

## Background

`jit search` with no `--glob` runs ripgrep over the whole data root (`crates/jit/src/search.rs:116-150`, CLI call site in `main.rs`), so it reads the event log and every gate-run record. The server always passes explicit globs and is unaffected. Verified with ripgrep 15: anchored negations do not apply when the search path is absolute, while unanchored `--glob '!events.jsonl' --glob '!gate-runs'` exclude both and keep absolute result paths, and a user-supplied `--glob` still selects gate-run files. The redo scratch directory can hold appended event bytes.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `repository_state/path.rs` declares the data-root history paths (the event log, the gate-run directory and the redo scratch directory) once, beside their `VirtualPath` constants.
- [hard] REQ-02: When neither a glob nor explicit file patterns are given, the search excludes each declared history path; an explicit selection is passed through unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: A unit test over a corpus shows that a default search returns no match from a history file and that an explicit glob still reaches one.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.
title: Default search reads no history file
